purpose: Compact review memory for DAv2-driven Vulkan performance canaries. This is not a production route table.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140 on RX 9070
entries.latest_observation: After stack-planned descriptor-pool leasing, the repeat-30 retained-pool wide4 bridge run completed with zero timed CPU fallback and sync readback. It measured about 102.7 ms mean / 104.2 ms median / 113.2 ms p95 in the cleaned validation run.
entries.decision: Keep as the current stable safe lane, but do not treat it as the sub-50 performance solution.
entries.next_proof: Use structural counters and GPU timestamp attribution to choose the next control-plane or FP32 linear plan optimization.

entries.canary_or_path: default stack-planned descriptor-pool lease retired on stack-exit submission timeline
entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140 repeat-30 and vitl_140 repeat-3 on RX 9070
entries.latest_observation: The repeated-request Windows stack overflow was traced to normal stack-planned recording allocating descriptors from the shared context descriptor pool while frequency submits were suppressed. Per-stack descriptor-pool leasing fixes the repeat-30 vits_140 failure and lets vitl_140 smoke runs complete.
entries.decision: Keep as default descriptor lifetime ownership for stack-planned recording. Do not replace it with eager descriptor_pool_.flush() at stack boundaries.
entries.next_proof: Add a focused regression test or budget gate when stack-planned descriptor counters are exposed directly.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140 on RX 9070
entries.latest_observation: A repeat-30 bridge run stayed correctness-clean with zero timed CPU fallback/readback/copy. sync_counters now exposes retired_resource_count=15415 and retire_cleanup_callback_count=4668, proving cleanup callbacks are flatter than per-resource retirement while submit topology remains unchanged.
entries.decision: Keep as a generic cleanup-control-plane fix. It is not a submit-reduction or shader-speed claim.
entries.next_proof: Use the callback/resource split to decide whether the next cleanup work should be a typed region/session cleanup executor or whether remaining latency is dominated by submits and kernel plans.

entries.latest_observation: Successful vision execution no longer pays recovery flushes unless a Vulkan API failure marked recovery required.
entries.next_proof: Regression gate should keep successful timed forwards free of recovery-path synchronizes.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140 on RX 9070
entries.latest_observation: Opt-in per-stack lease remained correctness-clean but was slower than the retained persistent-pool default and did not fix compiled_session_bridge exit -1073741571.
entries.decision: Keep opt-in for ownership experiments; do not enable on the hot path.
entries.next_proof: Only revisit if a concrete command/descriptor lifetime bug requires per-stack pool ownership.

entries.latest_observation: Repeated smoke tests still exit with Windows stack overflow -1073741571 before writing a result artifact.
entries.decision: Do not use for performance baselines or route promotion.
entries.next_proof: Isolate whether the overflow is C++ recursion, Python wrapper recursion, replay metadata growth, decoder compiled-session scope, or retained state across forwards.

entries.canary_or_path: repeated context-owned stack_capture_decoder_preprocess without segmented stack-owned recording
entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits/vitl bridge rows
entries.latest_observation: Repeated context-owned bridge execution can hit Windows stack overflow after one-repeat sanity passes.
entries.decision: Keep repeated benchmark runs fail-closed; use bounded segmented stack-owned modes.
entries.next_proof: Only revisit through a bounded region/segment plan with explicit output handoff and lifetime ownership.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 deeper bridge variants
entries.latest_observation: Native private-baton deep split is the allowed migration target for stacks deeper than the max-12-block proven rowset.
entries.decision: Keep as bounded canary path, not a model-name route.
entries.next_proof: Generalize by segment policy and verify on the five-model coverage corpus before default promotion.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 deep bridge probes
entries.latest_observation: Benchmark-mediated Python private baton can stack overflow before result artifacts.
entries.next_proof: Do not revisit unless the bridge is converted into a native region-owned transfer with explicit lifetime proof.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140 on RX 9070
entries.latest_observation: Correctness-clean and uses fewer stack-planned submits than wide4, but remained slower and kept the same retire-drain pressure.
entries.decision: Do not promote. Wider segments alone are not the current answer.
entries.next_proof: Only revisit after retire-drain ownership changes or command recording overhead is isolated.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140/vitb_140 on RX 9070, GTX 1080, and RX 6700 XT
entries.latest_observation: Both candidates were correctness-clean but mixed wins and regressions across model/device rows.
entries.decision: Do not promote as static defaults. Use as inputs to device/driver/plan-key tuning.
entries.next_proof: Build runtime tuning cache consumption or a full-row validated exact-plan policy keyed by VulkanConvPlanKey and capability profile.

entries.canary_or_path: broad label-inferred tiled float-buffer linear gate
entries.latest_observation: Corrected activation hit tiled kernels but failed bridge sanity with max_abs around 0.215.
entries.decision: Do not reintroduce broad tiled linear routing.
entries.next_proof: Develop a parity-proven FP32 linear kernel or narrower contract-backed candidate.

entries.model_evidence: Depth Anything V2 vits_140 on RX 9070
entries.latest_observation: Existing checked-in evidence records the exact fc2 tiled canary as correctness-clean but slower than the retained-pool wide4 baseline. The current local run did not provide promotable tiled-plan evidence.
entries.decision: Do not promote the current tiled fc2 kernel.
entries.next_proof: Use the GPU timestamp finding that fc2 is hot to design a new parity-proven FP32 linear plan candidate.

entries.latest_observation: Correctness-clean and preserves zero fallback/readback/copy, but uses the wrong release boundary for private bridge captures and does not remove retire drains.
entries.decision: Do not promote stack-exit private bridge capture handoff.
entries.next_proof: Move release ownership to post-decoder-consumer completion before any transfer canary.

entries.canary_or_path: default bounded stack-owned segment retire-drain deferral; set PYTORCH_VULKAN_STACK_REGION_RETIRE_DRAIN_DEFER=disabled for diagnostics
entries.latest_observation: After stack-planned cleanup callback batching, the bounded deferral gate removed all timed retire_queue_drain submits in a repeat-30 vits_140 bridge run while preserving correctness, zero timed fallback/readback/copy, and visible deferred pending-resource counters.
entries.decision: Promote the narrow stack-owned/current-thread/resource-budget deferral as default. It is still not broad retire batching or current-topology submit elision.
entries.next_proof: Reduce one of the remaining submit classes or attack the top timestamped GPU kernels; the timed path still has four stack-planned submits, one pre-stack flush, and one explicit synchronize per request.
